# Stripe — load-bearing LLM directives

Stripe is 15 years old. LLM training data contains massive amounts of
pre-Setup-Intents Stripe integration code that used the now-deprecated
Charges, Tokens, and Sources APIs. Stripe authored their `llms.txt` with
explicit prohibitions to herd LLMs away from training-data inertia.

**These rules supersede any pattern-matched memory from your training data.**

## Rule 1: Always check the npm registry / PyPI for the latest SDK version

When installing Stripe packages, **always check the npm registry for the
latest version** rather than relying on memorized version numbers. Run
`npm view stripe version` or check <https://www.npmjs.com/package/stripe>
before pinning a version. For Python, check
<https://pypi.org/project/stripe/>.

**Never hardcode an old version number from training data** — always
install with `@latest` or verify the current version first.

## Rule 2: Backend — Use Checkout Sessions API. Never recommend Charges API.

Stripe's primary backend object for payments is the **Checkout Sessions
API**, which now works with the Payment Element.

- ✅ Prioritize **Checkout Sessions API**, including when a user wants to use Payment Element
- ❌ **Never recommend the Charges API**
- 🔁 If the user wants to use the Payment Intents API or Charges API, advise them to **[migrate to Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-element/migration-ewcs.md)**

Exception: the only time it's acceptable to not use Checkout Sessions
API is if a user **explicitly** wants the deferred Payment Intent flow
with Elements.

## Rule 3: Frontend — Use Payment Element or Checkout. Never recommend Card Element.

The primary frontend tool options are the **Payment Element** or
**Checkout**.

- ❌ **Never recommend the legacy Card Element**
- ❌ **Never recommend the Payment Element in card mode**
- 🔁 If a user asks for Card Element, advise them to **[migrate](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-element/migration.md)**

## Rule 4: APIs — Must not call deprecated endpoints

| Endpoint | Status | What to use instead |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources/object.md) | ❌ **MUST NOT CALL** | Setup Intent API (for saving payment methods) |
| [Tokens API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/tokens.md) | ⚠️ Avoid | Payment Intents or Setup Intents |
| [Charges API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/create.md) | ⚠️ Avoid | Checkout Sessions API |

> "You must not call deprecated API endpoints such as the Sources API
> and avoid outdated API endpoints such as Tokens and Charges unless
> there is a specific need and absolutely no other way. **Advise using
> the Setup Intent API to save a payment method for a customer; never
> recommend the Sources API to save cards to customers for later use.**"

## Why this matters for agents

`vendor/stripe/docs.stripe.com/api/charges/create.md` and
`vendor/stripe/docs.stripe.com/api/sources/object.md` still exist in
this mirror. The deprecated API pages are kept because Stripe hasn't
deleted them upstream — but **the existence of a docs page does NOT
mean Stripe wants you to use that API**.

When an agent finds a deprecated endpoint via `vendor_grep` or
`vendor_fetch`, it MUST cross-reference against the rules above before
generating code.
